text: But his strength soon gave out. <break time="0.8s" /> And after falling many times. <break time="0.8s" /> He sat down. <break time="0.8s" /> And decided to meet death with dignity. <break time="0.8s" /> He pictured the boys. <break time="0.8s" /> Coming along the trail the next day. <break time="0.8s" /> And it seemed that he was with them. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking for himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Freezing was not as bad. <break time="0.8s" /> As people thought. <break time="0.8s" /> He told himself. <break time="0.8s" /> And he felt strangely warm and comfortable. <break time="0.8s" /> You were right, old hoss. <break time="0.8s" /> You were right. <break time="0.8s" /> He whispered. <break time="0.8s" /> To the old timer of Sulphur Creek. <break time="0.8s" /> In his mind. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he drifted into the most comfortable and satisfying sleep. <break time="0.8s" /> That he had ever known. <break time="0.8s" /> And he never woke again. <break time="0.8s" /> Never in its life. <break time="0.8s" /> Had the dog seen a man. <break time="0.8s" /> Sit like that in the snow. <break time="0.8s" /> And make no fire. <break time="0.8s" /> As darkness came. <break time="0.8s" /> It crept close to the man. <break time="0.8s" /> And caught the scent of death. <break time="0.8s" /> Which made it back away. <break time="0.8s" /> It howled once. <break time="0.8s" /> Under the stars. <break time="0.8s" /> That leaped and danced in the cold sky. <break time="0.8s" /> And then it turned. <break time="0.8s" /> And trotted up the trail. <break time="0.8s" /> It was going toward the camp. <break time="0.8s" /> It knew. <break time="0.8s" /> Where there were other men. <break time="0.8s" /> Who could give it food and fire.
